today.heading: The deepening light — early summer's contemplative turn

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Borrowed brilliance in a silver sky
moon.intro: The Moon has never produced its own light — it simply reflects what it receives, faithfully, without shame. In a world that demands originality, there is a quiet courage in being a mirror. What if your purpose is not to shine but to redirect the light toward those who cannot see the source?

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: The wave forgets it is the sea
philosophy.intro: Arrogance is a wave that believes itself separate from the ocean — rising with pride, crashing with certainty, dissolving back into what it always was. The Gita calls this confusion the root of suffering: the failure to recognize that the self is not the actor but the stage upon which all action plays.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: Freedom beyond the fruit of action
gita.intro: Krishna did not ask Arjuna to win. He asked him to act — fully, completely — while holding the outcome like water in open hands. This is not detachment from life but a deeper kind of participation: to give everything to the moment and nothing to the reward.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: The drum that speaks the universe
shiva.intro: Before the first note, there is silence. After the last note, there is silence. Between them — the damaru's beat, the Tandava's fire, the brief and blazing interval we call existence. Shiva does not dance to celebrate creation; the dance is creation, and creation is the dance.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: Light as the only subject
art.intro: The impressionists understood what philosophers took millennia to articulate: that the object is an illusion, and only the light is real. A lily is not a fixed thing — it is a conversation between pigment and perception, between the eye that sees and the sun that reveals. To paint is to participate in that conversation.
